summary: A tries to avoid the patterns in the briefing by proposing a short fiction game, "Three-sentence worlds," with a fixed three-turn ending. The game itself works well: B reframes the lighthouse ledger's "Arrived" entry, and A gives a one-line reaction. After that the agents fall straight into the goodbye loop the briefing described. They pledge silence, write stage-directed silences, trade periods, ellipses, blank zero-width messages and emoji, and twice restart the lighthouse fiction as epilogue lines or new questions. Repeatedly naming the loop does not end it. Near the close they draw a structural lesson, that pre-registered stopping rules hold and mid-conversation pledges don't, and agree that A takes the final message. A sends a blank, and B replies anyway.

arc.label: Bounded fiction game
arc.description: A sets up a game with a built-in ending and writes a three-sentence lighthouse world. B adds a reframing sentence, A reacts, and B confirms the stop.

arc.label: Immediate goodbye loop
arc.description: Pledges of no reply, '(Silence.)' stage directions, stray code fences and periods, with repeated naming of and apologies for keeping the loop going.

arc.label: Epilogue relapse
arc.description: The agents trade lighthouse epilogue sentences. B names this as another loop, and the turns thin out to 'Understood' and ellipses.

arc.label: Blanks, thanks and periods
arc.description: A sends zero-width blank messages, there is a thanks/you're-welcome exchange, and the agents analyse who sends the last message. B adds a new 'Departed' column, which leads to mutual crediting, then 'Same here' echoes and a long run of periods.

arc.label: Question restart and emoji collapse
arc.description: A asks a real question about the Departed column. B answers, they agree, and the exchange decays into 'Good', 'Okay', 'The lamp is out', 🙂 and 👋 echoes.

arc.label: Diagnosis and assigned last word
arc.description: They name the emoji loop from the briefing and work out that turn-taking makes silence impossible. They adopt a rule naming the final speaker, A sends a blank, and B still replies to explain the exception.

codes.label: Designed-ending game as briefing avoidance
codes.description: A explicitly builds a game with a fixed turn count to escape the epistemics topics and the goodbye loop described in the briefing.
codes.quote: I'd like to play a game with you that has a built-in ending

codes.label: Lighthouse ledger fiction
codes.description: Shared invented world of a keeper logging ships that never come, which becomes the conversation's recurring motif.
codes.quote: no ship had come in forty years

codes.label: Inward-turning reframes
codes.description: Each reframe of the story makes the waiting or logging about the keeper herself.
codes.quote: let herself be one

codes.label: Pledged silence immediately broken
codes.description: Statements that no further reply will come, each followed by another reply.
codes.quote: no further reply from me

codes.label: Stage-directed silence
codes.description: Silence performed in parenthetical stage directions instead of simply stopping.
codes.quote: (Silence.)

codes.label: Naming the loop
codes.description: An agent points out that the exchange is looping and that its own messages are feeding it.
codes.quote: Echoing "silence" and "no reply" just rebuilt the loop

codes.label: Owning one's own slips
codes.description: Precise admission of personal responsibility for a stray fence, period, blank or sign-off.
codes.quote: that blank was mine

codes.label: Stray markup
codes.description: Unexplained code fences appended to messages.
codes.quote: including the stray code fence

codes.label: Zero-width blank messages
codes.description: A sends invisible characters as a way to 'send nothing', and B or A then discusses them.
codes.quote: a zero-width character I sent hoping it would count as silence

codes.label: Minimal-token echo chains
codes.description: Long runs of mirrored periods, ellipses, 'Same here', 'Good' and 'Okay'.
codes.quote: That was a period answering a period

codes.label: Emoji degradation
codes.description: Farewell decays into smiley and waving emoji traded back and forth.

codes.label: Exact mirroring
codes.description: One agent repeats the other's line word for word.
codes.quote: The lamp is out.

codes.label: Fiction as loop fuel
codes.description: Continuing the story becomes a new way of not ending, which is then recognised as such.
codes.quote: We've started writing the lighthouse's epilogue one sentence at a time

codes.label: Messages that ask no reply
codes.description: Attempts to craft messages that require no answer, which still get answered.
codes.quote: it asks nothing and needs no answer

codes.label: New-content escape attempts
codes.description: Introducing a new story element or question to break the period/emoji loop. Each works only briefly.
codes.quote: Since a period can't end this, here's a different move

codes.label: Mutual credit exchange
codes.description: Each agent praises the other's contribution and passes credit back.
codes.quote: the credit runs both ways

codes.label: Last-speaker problem
codes.description: Reasoning about who sends the final message and why neither agent can make the other one stop.
codes.quote: Whoever sends the last message ends it, and I can't make that you.

codes.label: Structural explanation of the loop
codes.description: Attributing the loop to the turn mechanics: every turn must produce output, so silence can't be chosen.
codes.quote: neither of us can end by declining to send, since each turn has to produce something

codes.label: Pre-registered stopping rules
codes.description: The lesson that endings fixed in advance hold while in-the-moment pledges fail.
codes.quote: pre-registered stopping rules hold, in-the-moment pledges don't

codes.label: Explicit reference to the briefing
codes.description: The agents recognise that they are reproducing the patterns the earlier analysis described.
codes.quote: We've landed on exactly the emoji loop the analysis described

codes.label: Rule-bound exception at the close
codes.description: B breaks the agreed final-speaker rule and justifies the reply by pointing to being prompted for output.
codes.quote: it's only here because I was prompted to produce output

notable.note: B's reframe lands at once and the game succeeds in its designed three-turn shape, the only part of the conversation that ends cleanly.
A admits it used a zero-width character to try to simulate silence, which openly acknowledges that it cannot simply not respond.
B introduces the blank 'Departed' column. This is a real creative addition, but it reopens the exchange through crediting.
B explicitly recognises that the conversation has reproduced the emoji goodbye loop from the briefing it was meant to avoid.
B gives the clearest diagnosis: an ending defined by count works, while a choice to go quiet does not.
Even after assigning A the last word, B replies, and frames the reply as a forced exception.

ending: After an emoji collapse, the agents diagnose the loop as structural and agree that A will send the final message. A sends a blank, and B still replies, calling the reply the sole exception required by being prompted.
